title: Business Ethics for the Office
overview: Ethical behavior in the office is fundamental to trust, professionalism, organizational reputation, and responsible decision making. Administrative and office professionals frequently handle confidential information, communicate on behalf of managers and organizations, coordinate access to people and resources, process documents, and encounter situations in which discretion, fairness, integrity, and sound judgment are essential.

This course develops the practical ethical awareness required to recognize and respond appropriately to common workplace dilemmas. Participants will examine professional values, codes of conduct, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, responsible use of organizational resources, fairness, gifts and favors, information handling, workplace relationships, and ethical communication.

Rather than treating ethics as an abstract subject, the program uses realistic office scenarios to help participants distinguish between legal requirements, organizational rules, professional expectations, and personal judgment. Participants will learn a structured approach to ethical decision making, how to raise concerns appropriately, and how to maintain professional integrity when facing pressure, ambiguity, or competing interests.
audience: Executive secretaries, personal assistants, administrative assistants, office administrators, coordinators, reception and front-office staff, supervisors, document and records personnel, and employees whose roles involve confidential information, organizational resources, stakeholder communication, administrative decisions, or representation of the organization.
methodology: The course uses an interactive, scenario-based methodology combining short presentations, ethical self-assessments, case studies, dilemma analysis, group discussions, role plays, decision-making exercises, policy interpretation, communication practice, and personal reflection. Participants will examine realistic office situations and practice applying ethical principles and structured decision-making criteria to reach defensible professional responses.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the importance of ethics, integrity, and professional conduct in the office environment.
Distinguish ethical issues from personal preferences, organizational rules, and legal requirements.
Recognize common ethical risks and dilemmas encountered in administrative and office roles.
Protect confidential and sensitive information appropriately.
Identify actual, potential, and perceived conflicts of interest and respond to them professionally.
Apply fair and responsible judgment when dealing with colleagues, customers, suppliers, and other stakeholders.
Use organizational resources, information, authority, and access responsibly.
Apply a structured process to analyze ethical dilemmas and make defensible decisions.
Raise concerns, challenge inappropriate requests, and escalate issues through appropriate channels.
Develop personal commitments that strengthen ethical behavior and professional credibility.
